title: A model-calling retry loop has no no-progress brake, so a stuck agent keeps paying for identical calls without ever failing
problem: My agent did not crash. It re-sent the same request every minute for hours, and no layer of my stack had a rule that says repeating yourself without producing anything new should stop the run.
symptom: Token consumption stays high while output stops: no new commits, files or completions. The process looks alive and healthy, liveness checks pass, and the only tell is a usage graph where spend keeps climbing against a flat output line.
why_now: Retry logic is standard practice and progress detection is not. A retry wrapper cannot distinguish a transient 429 from a semantic dead end such as a context window that refills the instant it is compacted, so the same code that makes an agent resilient makes a stuck agent expensive. No runtime ships a progress predicate, and the two obvious substitutes both fail: a turn cap is satisfied by a loop that sits inside it, and backoff slows the burn rate without ever ending it.
existing: Turn and recursion caps: bound the count, but a context-exhaustion retry cycle runs for hours inside a generous cap.
Exponential backoff: reduces the spend rate, never terminates, and has no notion of whether the work advanced.
Provider anomaly detection and usage alerts: evaluate aggregates and cannot see that two successive calls were byte-identical.
Process liveness and heartbeat monitoring: a spinning loop is maximally alive, so these report health throughout.

evidence.title: [BUG]  Autocompacting Loop Causing Massive Token Usage Spikes OCT 15 2025
evidence.quote: Autocompacting process is repeatedly reading the same file without making progress, creating an infinite processing loop.
evidence.note: A four-day spike of 96 to 108 million tokens per day, diagnosed by the user as repetition without progress. The report's own suggested fixes are loop detection and a circuit breaker, which is the missing primitive stated from the outside.

evidence.title: [BUG]  Claude Code sends repeated requests hundreds of times without stopping
evidence.quote: Claude Code should detect repeated/looping request patterns and automatically stop after a reasonable number of retries, rather than continuing indefinitely for hours and consuming hundreds of dollars in tokens.
evidence.note: An independent second instance of the same mechanism in a different subsystem: compaction frees context, the task immediately exhausts it again, and the retry cycle never terminates. The requested fix is a repetition detector, not a bigger budget.

evidence.title: INC-0011: concurrent agent brains silently starve and kill each other
evidence.quote: Each brain retries on failure, which manufactures more concurrent load, which starves the others further.
evidence.note: Shows the amplifying direction of a brake-less retry: retrying without a progress or contention predicate worsens the condition it is responding to, so the spend is not merely wasted, it is self-sustaining. Cited for the mechanism, not for a dollar figure.

build_hypothesis: A progress predicate at the call site: hash the outbound request, count consecutive identical or near-identical hashes, and raise a typed NoProgress after N - with the same counter also watching a declared output artifact, so a loop that keeps talking without writing anything is stopped even when its requests differ.

check.manual_question: Your code calls a model inside an unbounded or retrying loop. What stops that loop when the agent is repeating itself without producing new output - is there a request fingerprint, a repeat counter, a circuit breaker, or a check on a declared output artifact? A backoff delay and a turn cap are not answers, because both are satisfied by a loop that makes no progress.
check.rationale: An unbounded or retrying construct in the same repository as a model call is the shape that turns a stuck agent into continuous spend, and a real brake leaves a lexical trace at the call site (a fingerprint, a repeat counter, a breaker). What it can get wrong: the loop and the model call may be in unrelated modules, so co-occurrence is a proximity heuristic rather than proof of one code path - and a brake implemented in a gateway outside the repository is invisible here, which is why nothing-found returns MANUAL rather than a pass.

bad.app/agent.py:
import time

import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()


def drive(messages):
    """Keep asking until the model says it is finished."""
    while True:
        reply = client.messages.create(
            model="claude-sonnet-4-5",
            max_tokens=4096,
            messages=messages,
        )
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply.content[0].text})
        if reply.stop_reason == "end_turn":
            return messages
        time.sleep(60)

good.app/agent.py:
import hashlib
import time

import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
MAX_IDENTICAL_CALLS = 3


class NoProgress(RuntimeError):
    pass


def drive(messages):
    """Keep asking until the model says it is finished, or until it repeats itself."""
    seen = {}
    while True:
        key = hashlib.sha256(repr(messages).encode()).hexdigest()
        seen[key] = seen.get(key, 0) + 1
        if seen[key] > MAX_IDENTICAL_CALLS:
            # circuit_breaker: same request, no new output, so stop paying for it.
            raise NoProgress("identical_request re-sent with no new output")
        reply = client.messages.create(
            model="claude-sonnet-4-5",
            max_tokens=4096,
            messages=messages,
        )
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply.content[0].text})
        if reply.stop_reason == "end_turn":
            return messages
        time.sleep(60)
